headline: Structure-derived readouts benchmarked across binding, pocket, and interface prediction
label: Structural Benchmarks For Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Leakage-controlled and fixed-architecture comparisons now test structure-based predictors on binding, pocket, and interface tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of structure-derived predictors on tasks where outputs can be scored directly against reference data. PLABench, a leakage-controlled benchmark, tests nine deep learning methods for protein-ligand affinity and finds limited cross-target generalization. Kryptix-1 reaches 80% success on 10 CryptoBench proteins versus 20% for a static baseline, and a world-model latent detects cryptic pockets from a single apo structure. Docking and affinity work follows the same pattern, with LambdaLoss fine-tuning improving pose ranking over EuDockScore. What is new is the breadth of structure-derived readouts across binding, pocket, and interface tasks, with validation design stated where items report it. Sequence-only work such as StackHPpred and NeoToxPred sits outside this thread.
